mainTopic: Items that may be sent on יום טוב (כלאים, shoes, תפילין) and wearing תפילין when the holy day begins
overview: This amud finishes the first chapter of מסכת ביצה. It begins by explaining that the כלאים garments the משנה lets one send on יום טוב are hard felt, which may be sat on. It then rules on other items that are free of כלאים: felt socks, coin pouches, and, according to רב אשי, even seed pouches, because nobody uses them to keep warm. Next the גמרא goes through the rest of the משנה's list of shoes. A spiked sandal may not be worn because of a past tragedy, though אביי proves it may still be moved. An unsewn shoe may not be sent even if it is pinned together. רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי each forbid a different color of shoe, and the גמרא shows they do not really argue, since leather was made differently in their towns. The משנה's general rule is then read to include anything usable on a weekday, which is why רב ששת let scholars send תפילין on יום טוב. Finally, אביי teaches what to do if שבת or יום טוב begins while one is wearing תפילין, and the גמרא settles two challenges to his rule by looking at how well the תפילין would be guarded. The chapter closes with the הדרן.

steps.title: The משנה means hard materials
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the כלאים garments the משנה allows sending are hard, stiff materials. It supports this with רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, who permitted the hard felt of נרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה is talking about hard materials. This is like what רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: this hard felt from the town of נרש is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its earlier question about how a כלאים garment could be useful on יום טוב. The answer is that the משנה means hard, stiff material.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the previous amud, the גמרא showed that even sitting on soft כלאים is forbidden, because a thread might wrap around the body. Hard felt does not wrap around a person or work like clothing, so sitting or lying on it is allowed. That gives the כלאים item a permitted use on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: A forbidden mixture, here wool and linen woven together (שעטנז)
Hard, stiff materials
Felt
Stiff or hard
It is permitted

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not say hard felt stops being wool and linen. The material is still in the category of כלאים. It is simply permitted to use in this way because hard material does not function like a garment.

phrases.english: Rather, it refers to hard materials,
phrases.notes: Answers the earlier question of what use a כלאים garment has

phrases.english: and this is like that which was said by
Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua:
this hard felt of Neresh is permitted.
phrases.notes: Permitted to sit or lie on, even though it contains wool and linen

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question asked on the previous amud about the use of כלאים garments on יום טוב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the משנה refers to hard materials
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to mean ordinary soft כלאים garments, which have no permitted use.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means hard felt, which may be sat on, so sending it on יום טוב is justified.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hard felt of נרש is permitted despite containing כלאים.

steps.title: Felt socks have no prohibition of mixtures
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that felt socks (ערדלין) are not subject to the prohibition of כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: felt socks have no כלאים prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another hard felt item that is free of the כלאים prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the idea from step 1 that hard material is not treated like a regular garment. Felt socks are stiff, so they fall under the same leniency even though they are worn on the foot.

keyTerms.meaning: Felt socks or felt shoes
They are not subject to the prohibition of

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
felt socks are not subject to the prohibition of mixed kinds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the hard-material leniency to another item.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Felt socks are not subject to כלאים.

steps.title: Coin pouches are permitted but seed pouches are not
steps.stepSummary: רבא draws a line: pouches for coins have no כלאים issue, but pouches for seeds do.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: these bundles for coins have no כלאים prohibition, but bundles for seeds do have a כלאים prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rules on two kinds of pouch and treats them differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Coin pouches are small and stiff, so they fit the hard-material leniency. Seed pouches are larger and softer, so רבא treats them more like ordinary cloth that could warm the body.

keyTerms.meaning: Bundles or pouches
Coins
Seeds

phrases.english: Rava said:
these bundles for coins,
are not subject to the prohibition of mixed kinds;
those for seeds are subject to the prohibition of mixed kinds.
phrases.notes: Seed pouches are larger and softer

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further ruling, this time drawing a distinction between two types of pouch.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Coin pouches are exempt from כלאים, while seed pouches are subject to it.

steps.title: רב אשי permits both kinds of pouch
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי disagrees with רבא and permits both kinds of pouch. His reason is that pouches are not used to keep warm.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: both this one and that one have no כלאים prohibition, because this is not the way people keep warm.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי argues with רבא and permits even the seed pouch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי gives a new reason that does not depend on how hard the material is. The כלאים prohibition is about wearing cloth for warmth, and nobody uses a pouch to keep warm. So even a soft seed pouch is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one
The normal way of keeping warm

steps.whatToRemember: There are two different reasons for leniency in כלאים. One is that the material is hard, as with felt (steps 1 to 3). The other, from רב אשי, is that the item is not used for warmth at all.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
both this and that
are not subject to the prohibition of mixed kinds,
because this is not the usual manner of keeping warm.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבא's distinction between coin pouches and seed pouches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both coin pouches and seed pouches are exempt from כלאים, because they are not used to keep warm.

steps.title: Why is the spiked sandal forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, which says one may not send a spiked sandal. It then asks why such a sandal may not be worn.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: but not a spiked sandal. What is the reason a spiked sandal is not allowed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks for its reason. This step sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A spiked sandal is a normal piece of footwear, and the spikes just make it sturdier. So it is not obvious why it should be forbidden, and the גמרא wants to know the source of the ban.

keyTerms.meaning: A sandal studded with nails or spikes
What is the reason?

phrases.english: But not a spiked sandal.
A spiked sandal, what is the reason it is not allowed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic based on the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a spiked sandal is forbidden.

steps.title: Because of a past tragedy
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the ban comes from an incident that once happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of an incident that happened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the ban on spiked sandals is a rabbinic decree made after a past tragedy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A disaster once happened involving people wearing spiked sandals on שבת. In response, חכמים decreed that such sandals may not be worn on שבת and יום טוב. So the rule is a protective decree, not a basic Torah prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident that occurred

phrases.english: Because of an incident that occurred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban is a decree made after a past tragedy involving spiked sandals.

steps.title: No wearing, but moving is allowed
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that one may not wear a spiked sandal, but one may move it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: it is forbidden to wear a spiked sandal, but it is permitted to move it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי separates two activities: wearing the sandal is forbidden, but handling and moving it is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the decree was only about wearing, it does not make the sandal מוקצה. You still may not put it on, but you may pick it up and carry it around the house.

keyTerms.meaning: To wear it as a shoe
To move or carry it

phrases.english: Abaye said:
a spiked sandal, it is forbidden to wear it
and it is permitted to move it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines how far the decree from step 6 reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A spiked sandal may not be worn, but it may be moved.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a decree against using an item in one way does not automatically forbid handling the item.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה's wording
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains both halves of his ruling. The ban on wearing comes from the incident. The permission to move comes from the משנה's wording "one may not send," which would be unnecessary if moving were forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is forbidden to wear it because of the incident. It is permitted to move it, as we learn from the fact that the משנה says "one may not send it." If you thought it was forbidden to move it, then since even moving it is forbidden, would the משנה need to say that sending it is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי proves that moving the sandal is allowed by reading the משנה's wording closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sending a gift requires carrying it. If even moving the sandal were forbidden, it would be obvious that you cannot send it, and the משנה would not need to say so. Since the משנה made a point of saying "one may not send," moving it must be permitted, and only sending it as a gift is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: From the fact that it teaches
One may not send (as a gift)
For if you were to think
Would it need to be said?

steps.confusionAlert: This is a "no need to say it" argument. If the משנה had meant that moving is forbidden, then forbidding sending would be obvious and pointless to state. The fact that the משנה bothered to state it shows that moving is allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: A spiked sandal may not be worn, because of the decree made after the incident. It may be moved. It may not be sent as a gift on יום טוב.

phrases.english: It is forbidden to wear it because of the incident that occurred,
and it is permitted to move it, from the fact that the משנה teaches: "One may not send it,"
for if it should enter your mind that it is forbidden to move it,
now, if even moving it is forbidden,
is it necessary to say that sending it is forbidden?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question meaning the משנה would not need to say this

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasons and the proof for אביי's ruling in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That a spiked sandal may be moved on יום טוב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's wording "אין משלחין," which would be unnecessary if moving were forbidden.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Wearing is forbidden because of the incident, while moving is permitted, as shown by the משנה's wording.

steps.title: Why say an unsewn shoe is forbidden? That is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that one may not send an unsewn shoe, and objects that this is obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Nor may one send a shoe that is not sewn.' But that is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, which forbids sending an unsewn shoe. It then complains that the משנה did not need to say this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An unsewn shoe cannot really be worn. The משנה only allows sending things a person can use on the day, so of course this shoe may not be sent. The גמרא asks why the משנה bothered to spell it out.

keyTerms.meaning: Shoe
That is not sewn
It is obvious. This is a challenge that a statement teaches nothing new.

phrases.english: And not a shoe that is not sewn.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה. The words 'one may send' are understood from the משנה's list.

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the משנה's list, after the spiked sandal.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's need to forbid sending an unsewn shoe
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An unsewn shoe cannot be worn, so it obviously may not be sent. The line seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Even a shoe held together with pins may not be sent
steps.stepSummary: The line is needed for a shoe fastened with pins, which can actually be worn.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed only for a case where, even though the shoe is held together with pins, it still may not be sent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The משנה is talking about an unsewn shoe that is pinned together and could be worn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this line, we might think a pinned shoe may be sent, since a person can wear it. The משנה teaches that it is still forbidden. A shoe that is not properly sewn is not normally worn, so it does not count as a usable item.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed only for this case. This phrase answers a 'that is obvious' challenge.
Even though
Pins or clasps

phrases.english: It was needed only
for a case where, even though it is held together with pins, it may not be sent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A shoe fastened with pins can be worn, so it should be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a pinned shoe may not be sent, because unsewn shoes are not normally worn.

steps.title: רבי יהודה adds that a white shoe may not be sent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's view in the משנה that even a white shoe may not be sent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Not even a white shoe may be sent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. This sets up the ברייתא in the next step, which will explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה adds to the list of shoes that may not be sent. The משנה does not say why white shoes are different, so the גמרא brings a ברייתא to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who adds a further restriction here
White

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Not even a white shoe.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף לֹא מִנְעָל לָבָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues through the משנה with a new opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a white shoe may not be sent on יום טוב.

steps.title: A ברייתא: רבי יהודה forbids white shoes and רבי יוסי forbids black shoes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives reasons. רבי יהודה forbids white shoes because they need chalk. רבי יוסי forbids black shoes because they need polishing.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה permits a black shoe but forbids a white one, because a white shoe needs a lump of chalk. רבי יוסי forbids a black shoe, because it needs to be polished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains רבי יהודה's reason. It also shows that רבי יוסי forbids the opposite color.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both rabbis use the same idea. A shoe that still needs work before it can be worn is not ready to use on יום טוב, so it may not be sent. They seem to disagree only about which color still needs work: chalk for white, or polishing for black.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
A lump of chalk, used to whiten the shoe
To polish it
A תנא who forbids black shoes

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Yehuda permits a black shoe,
and forbids a white one,
because it needs a lump of chalk.
Rabbi Yosei forbids a black shoe,
because it needs to be polished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רבי יהודה's line in the משנה and brings in רבי יוסי's opposite view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A shoe that still needs work before it can be worn may not be sent. רבי יהודה says white shoes need chalk. רבי יוסי says black shoes need polishing.

steps.title: They do not really argue: each followed how shoes were made in his town
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי agree in principle. Shoes were made differently in their two towns.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not really disagree. Each rabbi ruled according to his own place. In one rabbi's place, the flesh side of the leather faced down, toward the inside of the shoe. In the other rabbi's place, the flesh side faced up, toward the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the apparent argument between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי. Each was describing the shoes of his own town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The flesh side of a hide is rough. In רבי יהודה's town it faced inward, so a black shoe needed no polishing and was ready to wear. In רבי יוסי's town it faced outward, so a black shoe needed polishing first. The rule is the same for both: a shoe that needs work may not be sent.

keyTerms.meaning: And they do not disagree
Each rabbi ruled according to his own place
The flesh side of the hide
Facing down / facing up

steps.whatToRemember: The two rabbis share one rule: a shoe that still needs work before wearing is not ready, so it may not be sent on יום טוב. The different rulings come only from how leather was made in each town.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי argue about the law. The גמרא says outright that they agree. Only local shoemaking was different.

phrases.english: And they do not disagree.

phrases.aramaic: מָר כִּי אַתְרֵיהּ וּמָר כִּי אַתְרֵיהּ.
phrases.english: This Sage ruled according to his place, and that Sage according to his place.
In the place of this Sage, the flesh side was underneath,
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה: the rough side faced inward, so black shoes needed no polish.

phrases.english: in the place of that Sage, the flesh side was on top.
phrases.notes: רבי יוסי: the rough side faced outward, so black shoes needed polishing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא פְּלִיגִי. מָר כִּי אַתְרֵיהּ וּמָר כִּי אַתְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the apparent argument that came up in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Local custom: two different real-world cases, one rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי disagree about which color of shoe may be sent.
steps.terutzMaskana: They agree. Each ruled based on how leather was made in his own town.

steps.title: The משנה's general rule: anything usable on יום טוב may be sent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's general rule about what may be sent on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the general rule: anything that may be used on יום טוב may be sent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's summary rule. This sets up the story about רב ששת and the challenge that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ends its list with one rule that covers every case. The next steps test what 'usable on יום טוב' really means.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule
That one may use or benefit from
A Festival day

phrases.english: This is the general rule:
anything that one may use on a Festival.
phrases.notes: The משנה finishes: may be sent.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הַכְּלָל כֹּל שֶׁנֵּאוֹתִין בּוֹ בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the last line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anything usable on יום טוב may be sent on יום טוב.

steps.title: רב ששת allows sending תפילין on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת allowed the scholars to send תפילין on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת permitted the scholars to send תפילין on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports a ruling by רב ששת that allowed sending תפילין on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We do not wear תפילין on יום טוב. So this ruling seems to clash with the משנה's rule that only things usable on יום טוב may be sent. That clash sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who permits sending תפילין
Permitted
To send
Phylacteries

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet permitted the scholars
to send phylacteries on a Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real ruling that tests the general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תפילין may be sent on יום טוב.

steps.title: אביי objects: תפילין are not used on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב ששת from the משנה's general rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But we learned in the משנה that anything that may be used on יום טוב may be sent! תפילין are not used on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב ששת's ruling by quoting the משנה's general rule back to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the משנה allows sending only things a person uses on יום טוב itself. תפילין are not worn on יום טוב, so they should not be sendable. אביי says רב ששת's ruling goes against the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned in a משנה. This phrase opens a challenge from a source.
One may send

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But didn't we learn:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁנֵּאוֹתִין בּוֹ בְּיוֹם טוֹב — מְשַׁלְּחִין אוֹתוֹ!
phrases.english: Anything that one may use on a Festival, one may send it!
phrases.notes: תפילין are not worn on יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's permission to send תפילין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה allows sending only items used on יום טוב, and תפילין are not used on יום טוב.

steps.title: The rule means anything usable on a weekday
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the משנה: anything usable on a weekday may be sent on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: anything that may be used on a weekday may be sent on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי by explaining the משנה's rule in a new way, which supports רב ששת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'on יום טוב' in the rule describe when the sending happens, not when the item is used. An item counts if it is normally used on a weekday. תפילין are worn on weekdays, so they may be sent on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means. This phrase rereads a source.
A weekday

steps.whatToRemember: According to this answer, an item may be sent on יום טוב if it is usable on a regular weekday, even if it is not used on יום טוב itself. That is why תפילין may be sent.
steps.whyThisMatters: This reading makes the משנה's rule wider. It is the basis for allowing gifts like תפילין to be sent on יום טוב.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
anything that one may use on a weekday,
one may send it on a Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge and keeps רב ששת's ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only items used on יום טוב itself may be sent.
steps.terutzMaskana: Any item usable on a weekday may be sent on יום טוב, so תפילין are allowed.

steps.title: אביי's rule for wearing תפילין when the holy day begins
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that a person wearing תפילין when שבת or יום טוב begins covers them with his hand and continues home.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Since the topic of תפילין has come up, let us teach something about them. If a person was walking on the road with תפילין on his head, and the sun set, he puts his hand over them until he gets home. If he was sitting in the בית המדרש with תפילין on his head, and the holy day began, he puts his hand over them until he gets home.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new teaching. אביי uses the mention of תפילין to add his own rule about what to do if שבת or יום טוב begins while you are still wearing them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תפילין are not worn on שבת or יום טוב, but a person already wearing them is wearing them, not carrying them. So he may walk home with them on. He covers them with his hand so people do not see him wearing תפילין on the holy day.

keyTerms.meaning: The leather boxes worn on the head and arm
Since they have come to our hands, meaning since this topic came up
The sun set while he was on the way
The holy day began while he was there
He places his hand over them, to cover them

steps.confusionAlert: He is not carrying the תפילין in his hand. They stay on his head, which counts as wearing. His hand only covers them.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Tefillin, since they have come to our hands,
phrases.notes: Meaning: since the topic came up with רב ששת.

phrases.english: let us say a teaching about them:
If he was coming on the road with tefillin on his head,
and the sun set while he was on the way,
phrases.notes: So שבת or יום טוב began.

phrases.english: he places his hand over them
until he reaches his house.

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה יוֹשֵׁב בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ וּתְפִלִּין בְּרֹאשׁוֹ
phrases.english: If he was sitting in the study hall with tefillin on his head
and the holy day began while he was there,
he places his hand over them
until he reaches his house.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: תְּפִלִּין, הוֹאִיל וַאֲתוֹ לְיָדָן, נֵימָא בְּהוּ מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the topic of תפילין from רב ששת's ruling to start a new, related teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone wearing תפילין when שבת or יום טוב begins covers them with his hand and walks all the way home, whether he was on the road or in the בית המדרש.

steps.title: A teaching says he only goes to the nearest house
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב איקא challenges אביי from a ברייתא that limits the walk to the nearest house, not his own home.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב איקא objected: If he was coming on the road with תפילין on his head and the holy day began, he puts his hand over them until he reaches the house nearest the city wall. If he was sitting in the בית המדרש and the holy day began, he puts his hand over them until he reaches the house nearest the בית המדרש.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב איקא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict אביי. It says the person stops at the closest house, not his own home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said he walks all the way home. The ברייתא says he goes only to the first house he reaches, where he takes them off. Both sources describe the same two cases, so they seem to clash directly.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection from an earlier source
The house nearest the city wall
The study hall

phrases.aramaic: מֵתִיב רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Ika raised an objection:
If he was coming on the road with tefillin on his head
and the holy day began while he was on the way,
he places his hand over them
until he reaches the house nearest the wall.
If he was sitting in the study hall
and the holy day began while he was there,
he places his hand over them

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לַבַּיִת הַסָּמוּךְ לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ.
phrases.english: until he reaches the house nearest the study hall.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's ruling from step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's ruling that the person walks all the way home
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about the same cases says he stops at the nearest house, so walking all the way home seems not allowed.

steps.title: It depends on whether the תפילין will be guarded
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא deals with a case where the nearest house will guard the תפילין, and אביי deals with a case where it will not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a difficulty. This source is where they are guarded, and that source is where they are not guarded.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by splitting the cases. Each source is talking about a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the nearest house will keep the תפילין safe, he leaves them there, as the ברייתא says. If they will not be safe there, he may keep wearing them all the way home, as אביי says. Now both sources are true.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not a difficulty
It is guarded, kept safe
This one ... that one, splitting two sources into two cases

phrases.english: It is not a difficulty:
this one is where they are guarded,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא: the nearest house will keep them safe.

phrases.english: that one is where they are not guarded.
phrases.notes: אביי: no safe place nearby, so he goes home.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא דְּמִנַּטְרָא, הָא דְּלָא מִנַּטְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב הונא's challenge from step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): the two sources describe different situations
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא and אביי seemed to argue about the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is where the nearest house guards the תפילין. אביי is where it does not.

steps.title: If unguarded, why must the תפילין be on his head?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges its answer: in an unguarded case, even תפילין found on the ground may be brought in, so why does the case need them on his head?
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is a case where they are not guarded, why talk specifically about תפילין on his head? Even if they were lying on the ground he could also bring them in, as we learned in a משנה: One who finds תפילין puts them on and brings them in, one pair at a time!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. It argues that the unguarded case would allow even more, so the detail "on his head" seems pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה in עירובין teaches that a person who finds תפילין lying in a field on שבת puts them on and brings them in, one pair at a time, so they are not left unprotected. So if the problem is that the תפילין will not be guarded, the rule should not depend on him already wearing them. The next step answers this challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this case?
Placed on the ground
For we learned in a משנה
Pair by pair, one set at a time

phrases.english: If it is where they are not guarded,
why specifically when they are on his head?
Even if they were lying on the ground, the same should apply,
for we learned in a mishna:
One who finds tefillin brings them in, pair by pair!
phrases.notes: He wears each pair and brings it in.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דְּלָא מִנַּטְרָא, מַאי אִירְיָא בְּרֹאשׁוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that אביי's case is where the תפילין are not guarded
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In an unguarded case, the משנה in עירובין lets even found תפילין be worn and brought in. So the rule should not need them already on his head, and the detail בראשו would be unnecessary.

steps.title: Two different levels of danger
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. אביי's teaching, which speaks only of תפילין already on his head, deals with a place where unworn תפילין would be safe from thieves and dogs. The משנה, which allows bringing in תפילין found on the ground, deals with a place safe from dogs but not from thieves.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This source (אביי's teaching about תפילין on his head) is where the תפילין are protected from thieves and from dogs. That source (the משנה about found תפילין) is where they are protected from dogs but not protected from thieves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 21 by showing that the two sources are talking about different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In אביי's case, תפילין lying there would be safe from thieves and dogs, so one would not pick them up. That is why the rule speaks only of תפילין already on his head. In the משנה's case, dogs cannot reach them but thieves can, so a person may put them on and bring them in. The deciding factor is how much danger the תפילין are in.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This phrase opens an answer that splits two sources into different cases.
It is guarded or protected
Thieves
Dogs

steps.confusionAlert: The word הָא appears twice and means 'this one' and then 'that one.' The first הָא points to אביי's teaching about תפילין on his head, which is the more protected case. It does not point to the nearest-house ברייתא from step 19. The second הָא points to the משנה about found תפילין, which is the less protected case.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is where they are guarded from thieves
phrases.notes: This refers to אביי's teaching about תפילין already on his head.

phrases.english: and from dogs.
that one is where they are guarded from dogs
phrases.notes: This refers to the משנה about found תפילין.

phrases.english: but not guarded from thieves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source refers to a different level of danger.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי's teaching, which mentions only תפילין on his head, and the משנה about found תפילין seemed to disagree about whether unworn תפילין may be put on and brought in.
steps.terutzMaskana: Safe from thieves and dogs: leave them. Safe only from dogs: put them on and bring them in.

steps.title: Why the משנה needed to teach this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains what is new in the משנה. One might have thought that since most לסטים are Jews who would not treat תפילין with disrespect, there is no need to save them from thieves. The משנה teaches that we still worry about the minority.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: most robbers are Jews, and they would not treat the תפילין with disrespect. So the משנה comes to teach us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה's case of 'safe from dogs but not from thieves' is a real danger worth teaching about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Jewish thief would take the תפילין and keep them respectfully, so there would be no disgrace. Since that is true of most thieves, you might think the risk is too small to allow carrying. The משנה teaches that the minority of non-Jewish thieves, who might disrespect them, is enough reason to bring the תפילין in.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said. It introduces a wrong assumption the source comes to correct.
Robbers or bandits
They treat with disrespect
It teaches us. It introduces the actual new lesson.

steps.whatToRemember: תפילין may be put on and brought in on שבת or יום טוב when they are not safe from thieves, even though most thieves would respect them.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that concern for the dignity of תפילין is strong enough to take even a minority risk into account.

phrases.english: You might have said:
most robbers are Jews
and they would not treat them with disrespect,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the second case in step 22 counts as real danger and teaches something new.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the חידוש using the מהו דתימא / קא משמע לן pattern
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since most robbers are Jews who would respect תפילין, there is no need to save them from thieves.
steps.terutzMaskana: The minority risk of disrespect is enough, so they are brought in.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק ביצה
steps.stepSummary: This is the closing formula for the first chapter of מסכת ביצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק ביצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The first chapter of מסכת ביצה ends here with the traditional farewell line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the argument. It marks the end of the chapter and expresses the hope of coming back to learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. This is the traditional closing words of a chapter.

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter 'ביצה'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the תפילין discussion ends.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: End of the first chapter of מסכת ביצה.
